description.value: Access Gallery is a free, artist-run contemporary art centre founded in 1991, located in Vancouver's Chinatown on the unceded territories of the Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil-Waututh Nations. The gallery has provided early-career exhibition opportunities to many of Canada's most recognized contemporary artists and fosters critical dialogue through experimental and collaborative programming. All exhibitions and events are free and open to the public, making it a no-cost cultural stop for touring cyclists moving through the city.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms the address (222 East Georgia Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 1Z7) and that all programming is free and open to the public. The accessibility notes page explicitly mentions a self-contained gender-neutral washroom, confirming washrooms exist. No bike-specific amenities (rack, parking, pump, water refill, etc.) are mentioned anywhere on the site; the only parking reference is to limited metered street parking and a parking garage on East Georgia Street.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Access Gallery is a well-established, free-admission cultural attraction in Vancouver's Chinatown that has operated since 1991; it offers a worthwhile no-cost stop for touring cyclists and is actively programming as of 2026.
enrichment_extras.notes: Admission is free per OSM tag fee=no and website statement 'Our programming is always free and open to the public.' Within 120m of multiple bus routes; nearest SkyTrain stops are Main Street–Science World (650m) and Stadium–Chinatown (800m).
